title: Frontal Lobe Epilepsy with Electroclinical Dissociation and Discordant Imaging Findings: A Case Report
content: Frontal lobe epilepsy (FLE) involving the supplementary motor area (SMA) or opercular region often presents with hyperkinetic or focal motor seizures. Localizing the epileptogenic zone remains challenging when scalp-video-electroencephalography (VEEG) lacks a clear ictal correlate and neuroimaging reveals discordant findings. A 49-year-old male with a 32-year history of drug-resistant epilepsy presented with highly frequent stereotyped nocturnal and diurnal focal motor events. Seizures were characterized by a premonitory aura, followed by left hand dystonic posturing and left facial twitching lasting 10–25 seconds without impaired awareness. Previous neuroimaging showed a right uncal lesion, which conflicted with the clinical semiology. The patient underwent a 4-day continuous 128-channel MPVEEG monitoring following complete anti-seizure medication withdrawal (levetiracetam, clonazepam, and cenobamate). A total of 31 focal motor seizures were recorded. While the clinical semiology strongly indicated a right frontal lobe origin (SMA/opercular region), continuous scalp-EEG showed a normal background activity without ictal changes. This case highlights a striking electroclinical dissociation in FLE and emphasizes that typical clinical semiology should guide management despite negative scalp-EEG and discordant temporal lobe findings.
